extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and general readers of classical literary theory and translations (Aristotle, Longinus, Demetrius)
extracted.subtask_description: Catalog/description page for a collected edition of three classical Greek treatises on literature (Aristotle's Poetics; On the Sublime; On Style). Useful for readers seeking editions, translations, and summaries of the works' theoretical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aristotle's treatment of Greek tragedy (Poetics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle's Poetics contains his treatment of Greek tragedy: its history, nature, and conventions, with details on poetic diction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This edition presents a reliable text and an accurate, readable translation by Stephen Halliwell, with an authoritative introduction tracing the work's debt to earlier theorists (especially Plato), its distinctive argument, and reasons behind its enduring relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation of the sublime (On the Sublime / Longinus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay On the Sublime ... treats the appreciation of greatness ("the sublime") in writing, with analysis of illustrative passages ranging from Homer and Sappho to Plato and Genesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually attributed to 'Longinus' and probably composed in the first century A.D.; in this edition Donald Russell has judiciously revised and newly annotated the text and translation by W. Hamilton Fyfe and provides a new introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory and analysis of four styles (On Style / Demetrius)
rubrics_metrics.description: On Style ... is notable particularly for its theory and analysis of four distinct styles (grand, elegant, plain, and forceful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ascribed to Demetrius of Phaleron and perhaps composed during the second century B.C.; this edition includes Doreen Innes' fresh rendering based on an earlier Loeb translation, with new introduction and notes representing recent scholarship.
